QF.id: SEBI Guidelines for AML Standards, CFT and PF with KYC Norms_28

question.text: Under SEBI's AML/CFT guidelines, which of the following correctly describes the record retention requirement?

answer.text: Transaction records must be retained for at least five years from the date of the transaction, while customer identity, account files, and business correspondence must be retained for at least five years after the relationship has ended or the account has been closed, whichever is later
All customer identification and transaction records must be retained for at least five years after the business relationship has ended
Only records of transactions reported as suspicious need to be retained
All records must be retained for one year after the transaction date

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook applies two distinct retention timelines. Transaction records must be retained for at least five years from the date of the transaction. Customer identity records, account files, and business correspondence must be retained for at least five years after the business relationship has ended or after the account has been closed, whichever is later. The Trap: Applying the "relationship-end" timeline to transaction records (or the "transaction date" timeline to identity records) collapses two different rules into one and is incorrect. Each record type follows its own clock. Note: Limiting retention to only suspicious transaction records would leave major compliance gaps -- the five-year rules apply to all in-scope records, not just STRs. Reporting entities should implement a records management policy that tracks both timelines separately.
